headline: Natural gas rallies while hot US inflation hits gold and oil eases
paragraphs: Natural gas posted the largest gains today, jumping 2.80% to $3.31 per MMBtu (EUR 2.96) and extending its weekly surge to 11.79%. The rally has been propelled by unseasonably cold weather across the United States combined with a drop in domestic gas production.

Gold fell 1.46% to $4054.30 per oz (EUR 3629.00) following higher-than-expected US consumer price inflation, which stoked expectations of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and pressured precious metals. Meanwhile, crude oil softened, with Brent slipping 2.93% over the week to $91.85 per bbl (EUR 82.21) after the US downplayed further strikes involving Iran, alleviating immediate supply disruption fears.

Elsewhere, platinum and palladium held onto solid weekly advances of 3.80% and 3.32% respectively, though specific drivers behind their weekly outperformance remain unclear. For Irish firms, the easing of global crude benchmarks provides some cost relief against sharply higher gas prices.
